newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rejects China criticism of Radio Free Asia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rejects China criticism of Radio Free Asia.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday rejected Chinese criticism of the infant Washington-funded broadcaster Radio Free Asia and said its transmissions would continue.

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said on Tuesday the radio aimed "to meddle in other countries' internal affairs," and that "this action of the United States seriously violates the norms of international relations."
But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said: "We disagree with this criticism by China. Radio Free Asia is here to stay."
"We think the Chinese people ought to have access to information about economics, about politics, about Western culture and ideas, and that's what Radio Free Asia is all about," he told reporters.
Radio Free Asia, which began broadcasts to China last month, is mandated and funded by the U.S. Congress and broadcasts to a number of Asian countries in their own languages.
It is modeled on Radio Free Europe, which broadcast to the communist countries of Eastern Europe during the Cold War and is still operating although communism has fallen there.
Shen said the radio was "not advantageous to the improvement and development of Sino-U.S. relations," already battered by disputes over trade, Taiwan, arms proliferation and human rights.
